title: 2003 HMMT February Team Problem 1
statement: (a) How many \(k\)-configurations are there of a set that has \(n\) elements?

solutions.text:
An \(n\)-element set has \(\binom{n}{k}\) subsets of size \(k\), and we can construct a \(k\) configuration by independently choosing, for each subset, whether or not to include it, so there are \(2^{\binom{n}{k}} k\)-configurations.
(b) How many \(k\)-configurations that have \(m\) elements are there of a set that has \(n\) elements?
